messages:
ashwin: Heads-up — spotted doubled token charges for a handful of customers after yesterday's routing canary. Usually happens when a client reconnects mid-stream and the toolcall gets re-emitted. Example from logs (customer id redacted):

ashwin (log):
  [2026-02-10T14:22:13Z] session_id=SESS:abc123 route=eu-west-1 toolcall_id=null prefix_len=512 emitted: provisional_credit=120
  [2026-02-10T14:22:17Z] reconnect session_id=SESS:abc123 route=eu-central-1 toolcall_id=null prefix_len=512 emitted: provisional_credit=120
  ledger: later both provisional credits reconciled -> confirmed (ends up double-billed at customer level)

maria: ugh. we pushed a change to canary routers to relax session-stickiness (sticky_session=false) for load balancing reasons. did we also change resume logic?

ashwin: not intentionally. behavior looks like: client reconnects, router assigns to different host, router doesn't have previous last-prefix state so it re-issues the toolcall and emits provisional credit. ledger reconciliation later confirms both because both progressed tokens. it's specifically hitting older clients that don't send toolcall_id header.

devon: two quick ideas: 1) require/encourage clients to send an idempotency header like `x-toolcall-id` (longer-term). 2) router-side dedupe: synthesize a dedupe key from (session_id, prefix_len, checksum_of_prefix) when toolcall_id absent. downside: race/ejection if router loses cache.

sarah: telemetry/product angle — we need to surface provisional vs confirmed credits in the console so CS can see transientes. We should add a `billing.stage` tag (provisional|confirmed) on credit events and a dashboard panel showing provisional->confirmed conversion rate over 30m/1h windows. also a small ux tweak: grey provisional credits in usage explorer and make them expandable to see events.

maria: synth key idea is reasonable as short-term mitigation. but we need guardrails so we don't incorrectly drop distinct toolcalls. how about: only dedupe if reconnect window < 60s AND client IP unchanged or same tls peer cert fingerprint? that reduces false positives.

devon: storing last-prefix checksum in local router mem is cheap but can be evicted under pressure. We could push a very small Redis cache with TTL=120s keyed by (session_id) -> last_prefix_hash. Writes are O(1). Concern: extra network hop on hot path for every resume; but resumes are rare.

ashwin: agree on Redis TTL. implement flow: on toolcall emission if toolcall_id absent -> compute prefix_hash and push to redis with TTL 120s AND emit provisional credit with tag `provisional_key=prefix_hash`. on reconnect, router checks redis for same prefix_hash and if found, skip re-emitting provisional credit and mark resume_dedupe=true (emit metric). fallback: if redis miss, emit provisional as today.

maria: nice. also add metric: `resume.dedupe.success` and `resume.dedupe.miss.eviction` and `billing.provisional.emitted`. product wants alert if `billing.provisional.emitted` > 0.5% of confirmed credits for more than 15m in a canary region.

sarah: also we should track a histogram of `time_to_confirm` for provisional credits. if many never confirm within 10m, that's a signal of bug (or double-charge). dashboard panels: provisional rate, provisional->confirmed 10m conversion, top customers by provisional delta.

devon: edge-case: older clients may send same session_id across different devices -> same session_id + different content. we should only dedupe when prefix_hash matches exactly AND maybe a byte-length match. compute prefix_hash = sha256(prefix_bytes || prefix_len).

ashwin: example pseudo-check in router:```
// receive reconnect
if (client_headers.x-toolcall-id) { proceed_idempotent_path(); } else { prefix_hash = sha256(prefix_bytes || len); found = redis.get(session_id+":"+prefix_hash); if (found) { metric.inc("resume.dedupe.success"); // attach resumed=true, drop provisional emission } else { metric.inc("resume.dedupe.miss.eviction"); emit_provisional(); redis.set(session_id+":"+prefix_hash, "1", ttl=120s); } }
```

maria: rollout plan? small canary in eu-west-1 first (where we saw most hits), keep TTL=120s for now, monitor `resume.dedupe.miss.eviction` and provisional->confirmed conversion. revert if false-positives spike.

sarah: for the console: add a checkbox toggle to include provisional in totals (default off for billing view), and expose a table row per provisional event with time and route. Product will ship a note to CS about the canary.

devon: cost question on Redis ops — should be negligible (writes only on emission, reads on resume). we can shard keys by region. also add circuit-breaker: if redis latency >50ms, fallback to emit provisional (safe).

ashwin: I'll open a PR with Redis client code + metrics + small router switch flag `resume_dedupe_enabled`. plan steps:
1) add metrics + event tagging (billing.stage)
2) implement redis-based dedupe behind flag
3) canary deploy eu-west-1, monitor for 1h
4) expand after + verification

maria: please include tests for identical prefix but different small mutating payloads, and a load test that simulates router mem eviction to ensure no regressions.

deploy-bot: deploy started: router-canary/resume-dedupe-enabled -> eu-west-1 (GUID: d4f7b3) :rocket:

ashwin: thanks — will also add a console patch for provisional visibility. tagging @devon @sarah for follow-ups. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team, looks like a solid mitigation path. :white_check_mark:
